page.running_head: Animal. in dulcib. aquis Ordo I.

main_text.l: A. Icon est Salmonis ante partum, hoc est, uerni & æstiui, non satis probè expressa. B. uerò autumnalis & hyberni Salmonis, sub partum & à partu, (qui rostro recuruo ac maculis pluribus facilè dignoscitur,) effigies est, melius depicta quàm alterius: quæ emendari ad huius exemplum poterit; aliud enim non differt puto, nisi quòd rostrum ei incuruum non est, &c.

page.notes: Two woodcut figures of fish: A, a salmon before spawning, shown with an open mouth and scaled body; B, a salmon (Lachs) with spotted body and a hooked lower jaw. The caption lines in the printed heads are set in black letter-style initial capitals and were transcribed as printed. The caption in the body reads in old German-Latin spelling as printed; the word "uerni" and "æstiui" are as printed.
